items.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
items.statement:
For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite wedge quotient, all normally ordered wedges and the charts $W_A,W_0$ of the Statement.

[F1] The complete three-case straightening follows from the original Laurent divided-difference action and terminates with Laurent coefficients and fixed ambient interval and total sum ([[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]).

[F2] The contract of [[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]] gives $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, $C_N\ne0$, $\ker A_N=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$ and the quotient identification $W_N\cong\operatorname{im}A_N$. On the quotient $S_i=Q=q^2$.

[F3] The actual residue matrix and divided difference specialize at $q=1$ to $S_i=-P_i$, with $P_i$ the factor flip; the divided-difference term vanishes. Consequently $A_N$ specializes to $\sum_w(-1)^{\ell(w)}P_w$, the signed ordinary antisymmetrizer.

[F4] The vector rules are $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$, and $K_iu_m=q^{\delta_{m\equiv i}-\delta_{m\equiv i+1}}u_m$; the fixed coproduct is $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$ and $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[lem-the-level-one-vector-representation-has-a-perfect-crystal-with-lower-global-basis]]).

[F5] Over the local ring $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$, the tensor product of two divided-basis simple rank-one strings has a basis of divided highest-weight strings whose residues permute the tensor-basis residues; the normalized operators preserve its lattice and induce the crystal tensor rule and partial inverses ([[lem-rank-one-tensor-strings-have-the-crystal-limit-rule]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** the finite dominance and signed specialization proof establishes the field and Laurent bases; the rank-one cube calculation and local-ring tensor-string rule establish the complete localized crystal claim.

1.1 Spanning and termination. For any finite tensor combination choose a finite interval containing its indices. In each word the total sum stays fixed under [F1]. Among the finite set of words in this interval of that sum, order first the sorted decreasing prefix-sum list and then the increasing-pair inversion count. Each secondary balanced pair strictly decreases the former, while a leading adjacent swap decreases the latter and leaves the former fixed. The multiset can change in a secondary branch. Thus every branch terminates, either at zero from repeated adjacent indices or at a strictly decreasing tuple. The relations have coefficients in $A$, proving field spanning and Laurent spanning. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Field independence. For finitely many distinct normal tuples $I_k$, let $t_{I_k}$ be their raw tensors. Each $A_Nt_{I_k}$ is a finite Laurent-polynomial combination of raw tensors, regular at $q=1$. Select the finite union of all their supports as rows. At $q=1$, [F3] gives signed antisymmetrizations. The strictly decreasing raw row $t_{I_j}$ occurs with coefficient $1$ in column $j$ and coefficient $0$ in the other columns: distinct decreasing tuples have distinct index multisets. Therefore the square minor on these rows specializes to the identity determinant $1$ and is nonzero in $\mathbb Q(q)$. If $\sum_k c_k u_{I_k}=0$, [F2] gives $\sum_k c_k A_Nt_{I_k}=0$, so that nonzero minor forces every $c_k=0$. This proves field independence and, with step 1.1, a field basis for every $N$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Laurent freeness. Step 1.1 supplies Laurent spanning. Any finite $A$-linear relation is also a field-linear relation and is zero coefficientwise by step 2.1. Thus the map from the direct sum of one copy of $A$ for each normal tuple to $W_A$ is both surjective and injective, proving precisely the claimed Laurent basis. No implication from torsionfreeness over a nonprincipal ring is used. The separate positive span is free over $\mathbb Z[q]$ by the same independence. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 The exact rank-one cube. Fix a color $i$. The integer pairs $(i+ke,i+ke+1)$ are disjoint for every $e\ge2$. An empty pair is inert; a doubly occupied pair is inert because applying $E_i$ or $F_i$ makes a repeated adjacent index, whose wedge is zero. Its net $K_i$-weight is zero. A singly occupied pair is a copy of the highest-weight-one rank-one module. Changing a free bit shifts an index by one and keeps the word decreasing; the only possible obstruction is an already occupied partner, the frozen double-pair case. Hence each block of fixed pair occupancies is, in decreasing pair order, exactly a tensor product of these free rank-one modules. More explicitly, $F_i$ on a free high bit has coefficient $q^{\sum_{s<t}\epsilon_s}$ and $E_i$ on a free low bit has coefficient $q^{-\sum_{s>t}\epsilon_s}$, where $\epsilon_s=1$ for a high bit and $-1$ for a low bit and the sums are over earlier or later free pairs. Frozen pairs contribute zero. Thus the tensor cube identification is an equality of module actions. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Local crystal stability on every cube. Apply [F5] inductively to a cube with $r$ free pairs. For $r=0,1$ its divided-string basis is its ordinary basis. If the first $r-1$ factors have been written as a direct sum of simple divided strings with an $A_0$-basis whose residues permute the product basis, tensor each string with the final highest-weight-one factor. The finite calculation of [F5] produces a divided-string basis of each such tensor summand whose residues again permute its product residues. Its transition determinant is a unit of $A_0$, so the lattice remains exactly the $A_0$-span of the cube words, and the normalized operators act on these divided strings, preserve this lattice and permute its residues or send them to zero, with partial inverses. Induction proves these assertions for every finite cube. Step 3.2 identifies this lattice with the corresponding block of $L_0$; the block bases are subsets of the normal basis, and their direct sum covers every tuple. Consequently both normalized operators preserve $L_0$ and give the claimed crystal on its normal residues for every color. [F5, step 3.2, step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 The weight and integrability conditions. A normal wedge is a weight vector, since its raw tensor is one and the kernel is quantum-group stable by [F2]; thus the free local span decomposes by weights. It generates $W_N$ by step 2.1. For fixed color every tuple lies in the finite cube of step 3.2, a tensor product of finite rank-one modules; hence $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent on all finite linear combinations. Together with the operator stability, residue basis and partial inverses of step 4.1, this proves that $L_0$ with the normal residues is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 Conclusion. The normal wedges give the field and Laurent bases and the finite dominance termination profile; the exact rank-one cube action establishes the crystal basis on the separate local chart $L_0=A_0W_0$. The image of the positive tensor lattice is not identified with $W_0$ or $L_0$, and no triangularity of negative straightening powers at zero has been used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Remarks

The necessary ring correction has a concrete two-bit witness: for $e=3,i=1,N=2$, set $h=u_4\wedge u_1$, $x=u_5\wedge u_1$, $y=u_4\wedge u_2$, $z=u_5\wedge u_2$. Then $F_1h=x+qy$, $F_1^{(2)}h=z$, and $s=x-q^{-1}y$ has $E_1s=F_1s=0$. The unique string decomposition is $x=(1+q^2)^{-1}F_1h+q^2(1+q^2)^{-1}s$, giving $\tilde f_1x=(1+q^2)^{-1}z$. This lies in $L_0$ but not in the polynomial span $W_0$; field independence proves the latter assertion. Thus the literal previous polynomial-lattice claim could not be retained.

items.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
items.statement:
Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge $M$, the finite wedge spaces $W_N$, the connecting maps $\varphi_{r,s}$, the direct limit $F^{(M)}$, the three charts, the filtration $q^nF_0$, and the normalisation of $\Omega_M$.

[F1] The normally ordered wedges with strictly decreasing indices are a field basis and a Laurent basis in every $W_N$, and the straightening stays inside the index interval ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]).

[F2] $Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ inside the $j$-th slot is the loop operator; the residue of $u_m$ is $m\bmod e$ and $\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$ for $m=j-ae$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F3] The loop operator $Y=z$ itself shifts a slot by $-e$, so its $e$-th power shifts it by $-e^2$; simultaneous translations preserve local index differences and hence the finite wedge relations. The levels of the vector-weight differences and $\delta$ are $0$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** show the semi-infinite words stabilise and agree with the partition indexing, then compute the vacuum weights by summing the loop exponents.

1.1 Finite-stage spanning and ordered-tail stabilization. Start with a finite word of length $r$ and choose $S\ge r$ so that the last appended ground index $L=M-S+1$ is below all its original indices. Its image at stage $S$ has $S$ entries, all at least $L$. By [F1], its finite straightening is a finite sum of normal tuples $n_1>\cdots>n_S\ge L$. For each resulting tuple put $\lambda_j=n_j-(M-j+1)$. Then $\lambda_S\ge0$ and $\lambda_j\ge\lambda_{j+1}$, so extending by zeros gives a partition. Every subsequent connecting map appends ground indices $M-S,M-S-1,\ldots$, strictly below the normal tuple's last entry; that image is already normal and is the longer prefix of the same partition word. Thus every direct-limit element is a finite combination of partition words with a stable representative under these ordered-tail extensions. Maps with different finite codomains are not equated. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Direct verification of the vacuum weights. Let $M=te+r$ with $t\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\le r<e$, and put $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-[et(t-1)/2+tr]\delta$. It gives $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$. If $r>0$, subtraction of the formula for $M-1=te+(r-1)$ gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_r-\Lambda_{r-1}-t\delta=\lambda_r-t\delta$. Here $u_M=z^{-t}v_r$, so this is exactly $\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$ by [F2]. If $r=0$, use $M-1=(t-1)e+(e-1)$: subtraction gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_0-\Lambda_{e-1}+(1-t)\delta=\lambda_e+(1-t)\delta$, and $u_M=z^{1-t}v_e$ has precisely this weight. These integer identities also hold for negative $t$. The base value and this recurrence uniquely determine the weights for all integer charges. The partition label is consequently the stipulated $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, whose $d$-evaluation is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$ by the explicit datum; size remains the separate grading. No fractional change of an integer loop exponent or infinite unregularized weight sum is used. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Partition indexing and direct-limit independence. An eventually-ground normal word has $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ with $\lambda_k$ weakly decreasing and eventually zero; hence the $\lambda_k$ are nonnegative and form a partition, and every partition gives such a word. For finitely many distinct partitions choose a common prefix length $N$ containing all their nonzero rows and every position where two words differ. Each partition prefix is normal and has last index $i_N\ge M-N+1$. Its next appended index is $M-N$, strictly smaller, so every later image remains a normal basis word, and the distinct partition images remain distinct. If a finite linear combination vanished in the algebraic direct limit, it would vanish at some common later finite stage: a colimit relation uses finitely many connecting-map relations, which can all be moved to that common stage. Independence of the finite normal basis in [F1] then forces every coefficient to vanish. Together with step 1.1, this proves the partition basis without assuming that arbitrary finite words survive tail attachment. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

3.1 The charts and the topology. Each displayed chart is free on the partition basis over its own ring. Both $F_A$ and $F_0$ contain $F_{\mathbb Z0}$, and $F_A\cap F_0=F_{\mathbb Z0}$ coefficientwise: an integral Laurent polynomial is regular at zero exactly when it has no negative powers. Neither chart is identified with the other. A nonzero vector of the local $A_0$-chart has finitely many nonzero coefficients, each of finite $q$-valuation, so $\bigcap_{n\ge0}q^nF_0=0$. On each finite label component the completion of $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ is $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$, and inverting $q$ gives the field completion $\mathbb Q((q))$; the corresponding full-field component is $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$. Separately the completion of the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart is $\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$. The Laurent lattice has $qF_A=F_A$ and therefore supplies no separated $q$-adic filtration. These statements concern the componentwise completions stipulated in the Definition; no full infinite direct sum is identified with a finite-rank completed lattice. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. The charge-$M$ Fock space is the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces along the ground tails, with a basis indexed by all partitions, the three charts $F_A,F_0,F_{\mathbb Z0}$ are distinct free lattices, the separated topology is induced by $q^nF_0$ (never by $q^nF_A$), and the vacuum weights are $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$ for $M=te+r$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: Tail estimates: q-adic vanishing against the vacuum and finiteness of the weight strings
items.statement:
Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge-$M$ Fock space, its normal partition basis, the ground sequence, and the energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with the criterion $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0\iff m_1>m_2$.

[F1] Finite normal words have strictly decreasing indices. Straightening preserves cardinality, total index sum and residue multiset, and keeps all indices between the input extremes. Hence an $r$-factor word supported in an interval of fewer than $r$ integers is zero. In an interval of exactly $r$ integers there is only one possible normal $r$-tuple, whose sum is the sum of the entire interval ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]], [[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]).

[F2] $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0$ iff $m_1>m_2$. Also $u_m=z^av_j$ when $m=j-ae$; thus $z$ shifts an index by $-e$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], [[lem-the-q-wedge-relations-coincide-with-the-type-a-energy-braiding-kernel]]).

[F3] A charge-$M$ normal word has indices $i_j=M+\lambda_j-j+1$. Its size is the finite excess $\sum_{j=1}^R(i_j-(M-j+1))=|\lambda|$ once $R$ contains its nonvacuum part, and its label weight is $\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$. The simple roots are independent in the explicit affine datum ([[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** straighten finite filled intervals, using cardinality for an added factor and the changed sum for a replaced factor; use the maximum index and the preserved excess for the period operator.

1.1 Right-tail vanishing. Put $L=M-s$. By [F2], $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_m\otimes u_L)\le0$ is equivalent to $m\le L$. Choose $B\le m$ and truncate the filled tail at $u_B$. The word $u_m\wedge u_L\wedge u_{L-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B$ has $L-B+2$ factors, all in the interval $[B,L]$, which contains only $L-B+1$ integers. Every normal term of its finite straightening would have that many distinct indices inside the same interval, which is impossible by [F1]. Thus this finite word is zero, as is every longer prefix. Its semi-infinite image is zero and therefore belongs to $q^nW_0$ for every $n$ at each such finite stage (and to $q^nF_0$ in the Fock space). This argument concerns the whole filled tail; it does not assert that $u_m\wedge u_L$ alone is zero when $m<L$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 Finite shifts of $C$. Here nonzero weight means that $C$ is homogeneous of a weight $\gamma\ne0$: it maps a weight space of weight $\nu$ into weight $\nu+\gamma$. Write each $Cv_j$ as a finite sum $\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^av_k$. Since $Cz=zC$ and $z$ is invertible, $C(z^tv_j)=\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^{t+a}v_k$. Thus each term replaces $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $d=k-j-ae$ belongs to a fixed finite set obtained from the $e$ fundamental vectors; its coefficient depends only on $m\bmod e$. A term with $d=0$ would be the same vector $u_m$ and have weight shift zero, so its coefficient is zero by homogeneity. Choose $D$ bounding the absolute values of all occurring shifts. [F2, given, algebra]

1.3 Definition and gradings of $T$. On an eventually-ground word define $T$ by prepending $u_M\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-e+1}$ and replacing every old index $i_j$ by $i_j-e$. The simultaneous translation by $-e$ preserves the finite wedge relations: all residue differences and index gaps are unchanged. The new ground tail is again the charge-$M$ tail, so this operation respects local kernels and extending a representative by ground entries, and defines a linear endomorphism of $F^{(M)}$. At position $e+j$, its excess above the ground index is $(i_j-e)-(M-(e+j)+1)=i_j-(M-j+1)$; the prepended entries have excess zero. The old residues are unchanged by translation by $e$, and the new ground entries contribute zero residue-count deviation. Hence total size and label weight are preserved before and after straightening, by [F1] and [F3]. In particular $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component; this does not require a permutation of its partition labels. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.4 Finite label weights. If $|\lambda;M\rangle$ has fixed label weight $\mu$, then $\Omega_M-\mu=\sum_i n_i\alpha_i$, where $n_i$ counts the residue-$i$ cells. Independence of the simple roots in [F3] uniquely determines all $n_i$ and hence $|\lambda|=\sum_i n_i$. Only finitely many partitions have this size: each has at most that many positive parts, each bounded by the size. Therefore each label weight contains finitely many partition basis vectors. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Dual left-tail vanishing. The mirrored filled tail ending at $u_L$ is $\cdots\wedge u_{L+2}\wedge u_{L+1}\wedge u_L$, with an extra factor $u_m$ on its right and the mirrored condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_L\otimes u_m)\le0$, equivalently $m\ge L$. Truncate its left end at any $B\ge m$. The resulting word $u_B\wedge\cdots\wedge u_L\wedge u_m$ has $B-L+2$ factors inside the $B-L+1$ integers of $[L,B]$, so it is zero by the same finite normal-basis count. Extending that left end preserves zero. This is the reversed-interval version of step 1.1 and proves the dual exact finite vanishing and all its $q$-adic estimates. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Deep replacement. Fix an eventually-ground representative of a Fock vector. At a sufficiently deep slot its index is $m$, and the entire local block $u_{m+D}\wedge u_{m+D-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m-D}$ is ground. In a term of the insertion of $C$ at that slot, replace $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $0<|d|\le D$. This still has exactly $2D+1$ factors, all in $[m-D,m+D]$. Its total index sum is the ground block's sum plus $d$. By [F1] the only possible normal tuple of that cardinality in this interval is the complete ground tuple, whose sum is different. Every normal coefficient must therefore be zero. The block vanishes before it is wedged with the remaining factors, so the insertion is zero at every sufficiently deep slot; the cutoff is uniform for the finite shifts and, by taking a maximum, for any finite linear combination of representatives. These eventual zeros converge to zero in the separated $q$-adic topology. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 Nilpotence on positive size. On $|\lambda;M\rangle$, $T^k$ prepends $ke$ ground entries and shifts all old indices down by $ke$. The largest shifted old index is $M+\lambda_1-ke$, so when $ke>\lambda_1$ all indices of the resulting word are at most $M$. Choose a finite prefix of length $R$ whose remainder is ground and whose last ground entry is below every nonground index. Its ground sum is $S_R=\sum_{j=1}^R(M-j+1)$ and its actual sum is $S_R+|\lambda|$, by step 1.3. Every normal $R$-tuple with maximum at most $M$ satisfies $a_j\le M-j+1$, and therefore has sum at most $S_R$. Straightening preserves sum and the upper bound $M$, so no such normal term exists if $|\lambda|>0$. Thus the finite prefix, and hence $T^k|\lambda;M\rangle$, is zero. Equivalently the only normal charge-$M$ semi-infinite word with maximum at most $M$ is the vacuum, excluded by the preserved positive size. Since $\lambda_1\le|\lambda|=n$, $T^k=0$ on the size-$n>0$ part whenever $ke>n$. [F1, F3, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Geometric inverse. On a positive-size component choose $K$ with $Ke>n$. The finite operator sum $G=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T^k$ satisfies $(1-T)G=G(1-T)=1-T^K=1$ by step 2.3. This gives the claimed finite geometric inverse on every nonvacuum label weight and the resulting isomorphism for the tail recurrence; no inverse on the vacuum component is asserted. [step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the right and dual left filled-tail estimates by exact finite vanishing; step 2.2 gives eventual zero for every deep insertion of a loop-commuting homogeneous nonzero-weight endomorphism; steps 1.3, 2.3 and 3.1 give the size-preserving and label-weight-preserving period operator, its positive-size nilpotence bound and finite inverse; and step 1.4 proves finite label-weight components. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 1.4] ∎

## Remarks

- The estimates are proved here in the library's residue convention
  $c-r\bmod e$ with the ground sequence $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$; none of the
  two-sided-unbounded evaluation statements of the earlier finite ordered
  tensor theory is imported.

items.title: Semi-infinite wedges are indexed by partitions and the action gives the node formulas
items.statement:
Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge-$M$ Fock space with its partition basis, the finite-prefix action of the $u_m$, and the sub-diagram with smaller diagram as in the statement.

[F1] Normal wedges form a basis stable under straightening; inserting a new entry and straightening touches only indices between the inserted index and its neighbours ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]).

[F2] The stable-prefix limits exist and agree with the direct-limit operators: the connecting maps append ground tails and the deep-insertion estimates show the value is attained on a finite prefix ([[lem-the-fock-space-tail-estimates-give-q-adic-vanishing-and-finiteness]], [[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]).

[F3] A corner cell of residue $i$ of $|\lambda\rangle$ is exactly an addable $i$-node of the smaller diagram; the bijection between normal words and partitions is $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]], [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** evaluate the finite-prefix coproduct on a chosen entry, translate collisions into corner additions, and control the artificial boundary by renormalising the cutoff.

1.1 The bijection and finiteness of the node sums. The map $\lambda\mapsto(i_k)_{k\ge1}$ with $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ is a bijection onto normal semi-infinite words because $\lambda$ is weakly decreasing and eventually zero, and $i_k$ is strictly decreasing and eventually equal to the ground tail; a partition of size $n$ has at most $n+1$ addable nodes and at most $n$ removable nodes, so both sums in the statement are finite. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The $F_i$ formula. On a prefix of length $N$ containing the support of $|\lambda\rangle$, the coproduct action of $F_i$ shifts a selected entry $i_k$ to $i_k+1$, provided $i_k\equiv i$; if $i_k+1=i_{k-1}$ the resulting term has a collision and vanishes by the wedge relations, and otherwise the shift is exactly the addition of the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k+1)$ of residue $i$ by [F3]. The coefficient is the product of the prefix $K$-eigenvalues of the finite coproduct, which is $q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}$: a frozen doubly occupied $i$-pair contributes net weight $0$, and the singly occupied $i$-pairs are exactly the other addable and removable $i$-corners, ordered by content, contributing $+1$ for each addable corner strictly to the right (higher content) of the added node and $-1$ for each removable one. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.2 The $E_i$ formula. For $E_i$ the finite-prefix coproduct shifts an entry with $i_k\equiv i+1$ to $i_k-1$; if it collides the term is zero, and otherwise it deletes the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k)$ of residue $i$, whose smaller diagram is $\mu-\gamma$. The suffix $K^{-1}$-weight contributes the addable and removable $i$-corners of $\mu-\gamma$ strictly to the left (lower content) of the removed node; the single artificial boundary pair at the cutoff contributes the reciprocal scalar $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}$, and appending one more ground entry changes exactly this scalar to its inverse in the same way, so the renormalised operator $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}E_i$ is cutoff-independent and defines the stable limit by [F2]. The sign is negative because $E_i$ shifts down in the wedge. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 The toral operators. The paired occupation count gives $K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$: a doubly occupied color pair contributes total weight zero, while each single occupied pair contributes $+1$ or $-1$, corresponding to an addable or removable corner. The full label in the charge-$M$ space is $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$ from [F3]. Since $\langle\alpha_i,d\rangle=\delta_{i0}$ in the explicit full affine datum, evaluation on $d$ is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$, so $K_d$ acts by $q^{\Omega_M(d)-m_0}$. In charge zero $\Omega_0(d)=0$, giving $q^{-m_0}$. For general charge replace residues by content plus $M$. This is the degree-torus action on the explicit label; it is not a simultaneous translation of all wedge indices by the loop operator. [step 2.1, step 2.2, F3, given, algebra]

items.title: The level-one partition Fock space and node residues
items.statement: Let F=⊕_(partitions lambda) Q(q)|lambda> with its chosen charge0 weight Lambda0−Σ m_i(lambda)alpha_i and size grading. Node(r,c) has residue c−r mod e. The vacuum is empty; F_i adds and E_i removes with the preceding explicit finite node formulas. K_i eigenvalues are proved by the node-count lemma; K_d acts by q^−m0. These are declared linear operators until the affine-relation theorem proves the module structure. A partition is e-regular iff each positive part has multiplicity<e; it is e-restricted iff lambda_r−lambda_(r+1)<e for every r, equivalently its CONJUGATE has part multiplicities<e. A column of height e is allowed in an e-restricted partition. Full Fock/crystal vertices are ALL partitions; the empty component will be the e-regular subset.
items.strategy: Transport the algebraic wedge basis along the proved beta-number bijection. The root/size/d labels and residues are literal corner computations, including the0-edge loop shift. The regular/restricted equivalence follows from lambda_r−lambda_(r+1) being the multiplicity of the column height r in lambda-prime. For example(1^e) is e-restricted but not e-regular. The affine relation/crystal results below establish the actual representations, not a silent assumption in this Definition.

items.title: The addable-minus-removable node count is the level-one Cartan pairing
items.statement: For every partition lambda and every i in I, with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable i-nodes minus the number of removable i-nodes of lambda, one has N_i(lambda)=delta_{i,0}-sum_j a_ij m_j(lambda). Consequently sum_i N_i(lambda)=1, the toral operator K_i acts on |lambda> by q^{<h_i,wt(|lambda>)>}=q^{N_i(lambda)}, and the central element K_0K_1...K_{e-1} acts by q, so wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j alpha_j has level 1 and the toral action is the one required for F to be a U_q-module. In particular N_i(empty)=delta_{i,0}, and adding a node of residue k changes N_i by -a_ik, hence changes wt by -alpha_k.
items.strategy: Induct on the number of nodes: the empty partition has one addable node, of residue 0, so N_i(empty)=delta_{i0}. If mu is obtained from lambda by adding a residue-k node, the addable and removable i-node counts change by the standard local rule: the new node appears as a removable i-node only if i=k, and exactly the addable/removable nodes of lambda adjacent along the rim change status; bookkeeping the corners of the skew shape mu/lambda gives N_i(mu)-N_i(lambda)=-a_ik=-(2delta_{ik}-delta_{i,k+1}-delta_{i,k-1}). This is the local form of the identity and iterates from the empty partition. Equivalent formulations are Leclerc Exercise 16 (t_i|lambda>=q^{N_i(lambda)}|lambda> with N_i the addable-minus-removable count) and the standard colored-Young-diagram weight computation of Misra-Miwa sec. 2 (wt(lambda)=Lambda_0-sum m_i alpha_i). The consequence sum_i N_i(lambda)=1 is the row-sum identity of the affine Cartan matrix together with delta_{i0}-sum_j a_ij m_j summing to 1.

items.title: Fixed-residue node cubes realize the actual Fock strings
items.statement: For the declared charge0 node operators, fix i and one partition. The orbit obtained by toggling its addable/removable i-cells is a FINITE BOOLEAN cube: availability of one such cell is unchanged by every other i-toggle, including e2. Put the slots in DECREASING content order, state+=addable/top and state−=removable/bottom. The node operators on this cube are exactly V(1)^tensor k for the FIXED rank-one coproduct, with K=q^(#plus−#minus). Its raw A0 partition span is therefore stable under the actual normalized string operators. In that order cancel +−, take f FIRST surviving+, e LAST surviving−; equivalently in the fixed increasing-content order cancel−+, take f LAST+, e FIRST−. Residue labels are all cube vertices, both endpoints are included, and epsilon/phi are the surviving minus/plus counts. The standard partition-orthonormal form is the normalized rank-one polarization, and all divided E/F powers have Laurent-integral matrices. No Chevalley minimum argument is used.
items.strategy: A corner's addability/removability is determined solely by its horizontal/vertical neighbors, whose residues are i±1 and never i for e≥2. Toggling another i-cell does not change any such neighbor, nor creates a new i-slot. Every subset of the finite slots can therefore be toggled, giving all2^k distinct partition diagrams. With slots decreasing in content, the iterated DeltaF coefficient at slotj is q^sum_(slots beforej)weight and the DeltaE coefficient is q^−sum_(slots afterj)weight; these are precisely N_r and−N_l of the node formula because other slots are unchanged. Hence the map from tensor bit vectors to partitions is a rank-one module isomorphism. Apply the already-proved rank-one tensor crystal theorem; its strict f/non-strict e rule unrolls to the stated cancellation/extremes, including zero endpoints. This proves exact A0 stability before any congruence is transported. Divided coproducts give Laurent Gaussian/integer matrices on these fundamental bit factors. For polarization, (F_i lambda,mu)=q^Nr, whereas sigma(F_i)=q^-1 K_i E_i givesq^(N_i(lambda)−1−Nl)=q^Nr; K is self-adjoint. Thus the standard delta Gram is the normalized form, with local perfectness; field and crystal operators are distinguished.

items.title: Good and cogood nodes by residue-signature reduction
items.statement: For an i-node word in the fixed INCREASING-content order write+=(addable),−=(removable), cancel adjacent−+ until no such pair remains. Surviving minuses are normal REMOVABLE nodes and the FIRST surviving minus is the good node for e_i; surviving pluses are conormal ADDABLE nodes and the LAST surviving plus is the cogood node for f_i. Missing chosen sign means the operator is0. Equivalently read DECREASING content/columns (top-to-bottom), cancel+−, take good=LAST− and cogood=FIRST+. These name conventions match the usual Fayers good deletion/cogood addition. They are combinatorial string data, not a selection by minimum ordinary Chevalley exponent.
items.strategy: Unique reduction follows by the stack matching of−+; any two local deletions commute or share no cancellable pair, so the matching survivors do not depend on deletion order. Reverse the word to obtain+− with first/last exchanged. The fixed-residue cube supplies the actual operator interpretation and both endpoints; no existence/module assertion is needed in this Definition. At e3 lambda2,i2 the two pluses choose the top-right cell(1,3), not the native leftmost opening at(2,1). At lambda21,i2 the minus-plus pair cancels; F2|21> may be nonzero but tilde f2 is0. items.statement: The constructed node operators on ALL partition vectors give a chosen P-graded integrable U_q(affine sl_e)-module for the fixed coproduct/Cartan datum. items.title: The empty partition generates an integrable highest weight submodule of highest weight Lambda_0
items.statement:
In the charge-$0$ partition Fock space the vacuum $\varnothing$ has
$E_i\varnothing=0$, $K_i\varnothing=q^{\delta_{i0}}\varnothing$ and
$K_d\varnothing=\varnothing$, so its weight is $\Lambda_0$. The nonzero cyclic
submodule $M:=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle$ is the simple integrable
highest weight module $V(\Lambda_0)$; its integral lattice is
$U_A^-|\varnothing\rangle$ for $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its crystal is the
empty graph component, identified in
[[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]]
rather than equated with the module.
items.strategy: Read E/K/Kd vacuum data from the finite node formulas. The cyclic vacuum submodule inherits ambient integrability; the actual early universal integrable highest theorem gives the normalized nonzero map V(Lambda0) to this cyclic module, surjective by generation and injective by ordinary simplicity of the source. Obtain the integral U_A^- vacuum lattice from integral divided-power tensor-cube coproduct actions and its field spanning. No unsupported maximal-weight argument for arbitrary submodules is used; the later crystal theorem supplies the graph identification.

items.title: The crystal of the level-one Fock space is the good-node partition graph
items.statement: The WHOLE level-one Fock module has the crystal basis(F0,B_F), F0=⊕_(ALL partitions)A0|lambda>, B_F={|lambda>+qF0}. The actual normalized Kashiwara operators REMOVE the good normal i-node and ADD the cogood conormal i-node of the corrected signature; epsilon/phi are survivor counts. This is a graph on ALL partitions, not only regular ones. Its empty connected component is precisely the e-regular partitions; e-restricted labels belong to the transposed model. A pole or a unique Chevalley term does not determine the crystal arrow.
items.strategy: Each fixed-residue block is the finite tensor bit module of the local cube supplier, so its raw A0 basis is stable under string operators and has the stated residue rule, including both endpoints. The full module is generated over the field by this free weight-graded lattice and satisfies the quantum relations; all crystal axioms follow blockwise and the weight formula is the node-count lemma. To identify the empty component, use DECREASING-content order. Removing the selected LAST minus could violate regularity only if it creates e equal rows of lengthL−1; then below its removable row lies a block of e−1 rows of lengthL−1 and their last corner is a consecutive same-residue minus. If the upper minus survives so does this lower one, so the upper one cannot be selected. Adding the FIRST plus could violate regularity only if a block of e−1 rows of the new length lies immediately above it; that block's first addable corner is a consecutive same-residue plus. If the lower plus survives the earlier one does too, so it is not selected. Thus both operators preserve e-regularity. Every nonempty regular partition has a top equal-row block of heighta<e; its first removable corner has residueL−a, while the only earlier addable corner has residueL, so its minus has no matching same-residue plus and survives. Some good deletion therefore exists, remains regular and lowers size. Induction and the inverse axiom reach every regular partition from empty. Since empty is regular and all adjacent edges preserve regularity, this proves exactly the component, without an abstract rank-one recognition assumption or an imported MM path count.

items.title: The semi-infinite action on the Fock space is well defined and the Fock space is an integrable U_q(ŝl_e)-module
items.statement:
The stable prefix operators on the charge-$M$ algebraic wedge direct limit give
a well-defined integrable action of the affine quantum algebra, proved from the
node formulas and all defining relations of
[[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]].
Infinite coproduct expressions converge $q$-adically and in this type-A model
have finite stabilised outputs; no two-sided-unbounded evaluation statement is
imported. On the vacuum $E_i\varnothing=0$, $F_i$ creates the single node of
residue $M$ and $K_i$ acts by $q^{\delta_{i\equiv M}}$. The wedge product of a
finite prefix with its correctly charged tail is $U_q$-linear with the fixed
formulas

$$E(v\wedge u)=Ev\wedge K_i^{-1}u+v\wedge Eu,\qquad F(v\wedge u)=Fv\wedge u+K_iv\wedge Fu .$$

With the declared use of the Axiom of Choice only in the general integrable
decomposition, the finite-weight upper cone of $F$ is a locally weight-finite
direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules; completeness does not
mean finitely many constituents.
items.strategy: Use the actual tail estimates to prove stabilization of finite-prefix coproducts and q-adic convergence to the original algebraic wedge space; splitting the fixed coproduct at the correctly charged tail gives the displayed wedge product and vacuum formulas. For each color use its finite tensor cubes to prove both local nilpotence directions on vectors. Independence of the full affine simple roots makes a label fix the residue counts and partition size, hence finite weight spaces; support lies in Omega_M-Q+. Apply the actual bounded-above semisimplicity supplier with precisely those finite-weight and finite-cone hypotheses and declared AC, obtaining a locally weight-finite algebraic direct sum without claiming finitely many constituents.

items.title: The empty component is the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0)
items.statement: With the declared AC for the general integrable-module decomposition, the empty component of the full partition crystal is the canonical B(Lambda0), with exactly the e-regular labels. Its module is M=U_q|empty> and its lower A0 lattice is M∩F0. It occurs once. More precisely F=⊕_(k≥0)V(Lambda0−k delta)^⊕p(k), a LOCALLY WEIGHT-FINITE indexed direct sum, where p(k) counts ordinary partitions of k. Hence chF=chV(Lambda0)Π_(r≥1)(1−exp(−r delta))^-1. A highest CRYSTAL label need not be a highest FIELD standard vector; the ambient canonical basis need not split these summands.
items.strategy: The full Fock module has finite label spaces and supportLambda0−Q+; its full crystal basis was proved from cubes. Apply the actual7 top-isotypic lattice/residue splitting and indexed decomposition. The highest weightLambda0 space is1-dimensional with vacuum, so its isotypic submodule is the simple M of the preceding proposition and its component is the canonical B(Lambda0); the direct combinatorial proof gives the regular labels. For all other highest vertices, inspect boundary signs by top-to-bottom decreasing content: for the top block of a equal rows of lengthL, the only earlier plus has residueL and its removable minus has residueL−a. If all minuses are canceled, a must be divisible by e. Cancel this block's matching pair and repeat with each next block. Conversely every block with multiplicity divisible by e pairs its own plus/minus, so all e_i residues vanish. Thus highest labels are exactly partitions formed by repeating each row of an ordinary partition rho e times. Each residue occurs|rho| times, giving weightLambda0−|rho|delta; there arep(k) such labels. The decomposition theorem identifies their field constituents and multiplicities, giving the full formula/character. This does not call those raw standard vectors field-highest. AC is used only through the already-declared decomposition/top-lift selection; all finite sign computations are choice-free.

items.title: The regular-partition label convention and the Mullineux crystal involution
items.statement:
A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.
items.strategy: Twist the normalized simple integrable highest module by the datum reflection and use its normalized universality to obtain the Q(q)-linear algebra-semilinear intertwiner fixing the vacuum. Its square fixes the cyclic generator and is identity. Unique string decompositions give color-reflected Kashiwara naturality, and the canonical A0 span of iterated Kashiwara lowering words is preserved; the resulting fixed residue map proves path independence. Verify reflected weights and distinguish conjugation between the regular/restricted models from the same-model Mullineux involution.

items.title: The basic representation global basis is unitriangular in the partition basis
items.statement:
There is an explicit semi-infinite wedge bar $\psi$ with the vacuum fixed,
coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $U_q$/bar compatibility, whose restriction
to $M=V(\Lambda_0)$ is the normalized highest module bar. On **all** partitions
its integral triangular correction is

$$G(\lambda)=|\lambda\rangle+\sum_{\mu\ \text{strictly dominated by}\ \lambda}d_{\mu,\lambda}(q)|\mu\rangle, \qquad d_{\mu,\lambda}\in q\mathbb Z[q],$$

with diagonal $1$ and same $e$-core support; the family $\{G(\lambda)\}$ is an
$A$-basis of $F_A$ and an $A_0$-basis of $F_0$, with the actual infinity chart
and balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection. Exactly the $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ form
the lower global basis of $M$, identified by the two lower-global-basis
suppliers. The ambient basis is not automatically compatible with the other
field irreducible summands. The transpose equality
$d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ is **false** in general; the source symmetry
concerns the bar matrix, not $D$. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use
$(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients require the restricted Gram
inverse and need not be Laurent polynomials.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Fock space with its partition basis, the wedge bar, the dominance order, and the lower global basis of the highest weight module $M$.

[F1] Finite normalized bar on a raw length-$r$ wedge is $\psi_r(u_I)=(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}q^{t(I)}u_{\mathrm{reverse}\,I}$ with $t(I)$ the number of unequal-residue pairs of the actual indices; it preserves the full two-factor kernel and is an involution, and its exponent identities $\psi F_i\psi^{-1}$ match the reversed suffix exponents ([[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]], [[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]).

[F2] Finite straightening preserves the total index sum, keeps indices between their input extremes, and has normal words with strictly decreasing indices ([[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]], [[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]). The truncation-independence argument is supplied locally in step 2.2.

[F3] The divided node matrices are Laurent-integral, the lower global basis of $M$ exists and is unique, and its crystal residues are the regular labels ([[lem-fixed-residue-node-cubes-realize-fock-i-strings-and-crystal-lattices]], [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]).

[F4] Dominance and conjugation are the published prefix-sum order and the transpose map; the $e$-core of a partition is determined by the residue counts ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-regular-partition-label-convention-and-mullineux-crystal-involution]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** solve the triangular bar equations degree by degree, prove prefix independence, then identify the regular part with the module lower basis and compare the two matrix symmetries.

1.1 The normalized finite reversal bar. For a length-$r$ tuple $I$, put $t(I)$ equal to its number of unequal-residue pairs and define $\psi_r(u_I)=(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}q^{t(I)}u_{\operatorname{reverse}I}$, extended by $q\mapsto q^{-1}$. This descends through the finite straightening relations: an equal-residue swap relation reverses to itself, whereas every distinct-residue two-factor relation reverses, after coefficient bar, to $q$ times that relation. For the recursive relation its four terms are $u_l\wedge u_m+q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l+u_{m-b}\wedge u_{l+b}+q^{-1}u_{l+b}\wedge u_{m-b}$; reversal and coefficient bar give precisely $q$ times these same four terms. All terms preserve the residue multiset, so the global factor $q^{t(I)}$ is identical on the terms of a relation in a longer word. Thus the relation ideal is preserved. Applying reversal twice cancels the barred scalar and gives $\psi_r^2=1$. For the finite action the residue-count difference under a lowering move is $t(I^+)-t(I)=n_i-n_{i+1}-1$, and under its raising reverse it is $-(n_i-n_{i+1})-1$; substituting these identities into the fixed prefix coproduct converts its coefficient bar to the reversed suffix coproduct. Hence $\psi_r$ intertwines the generator bar, and its toral compatibility follows from weight preservation. These are finite computations in the relations of [F1]. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Integral dominance triangularity. Straighten the reversed tuple of a normal wedge. The leading swap scalars cancel $(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}q^{t(I)}$, leaving the original wedge with coefficient $1$. Every other branch replaces an unequal pair by strictly more balanced interior indices with the same sum and residues. The sorted prefix sums therefore strictly decrease, so the corresponding partition is strictly dominated by the original one. All coefficients are Laurent integral and residues are preserved. Consequently on a finite degree the matrix of $\psi$ is dominance-unitriangular over $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. This conclusion is obtained from the finite relations, rather than assumed for the bar-correction equations. [step 1.1, F1, F4, algebra]

2.2 Prefix independence and the charts. Let $m$ exceed the partition size and move a new minimum $u_{-m}$ through the prefix. Every secondary correction removes that minimum and leaves $m+1$ indices above $-m$ with total sum bounded by the ground sum plus size minus $m$, which is smaller than the minimum possible sum of $m+1$ distinct integers above $-m$; hence all secondary branches vanish because no normal tuple with that preserved sum exists by [F2], only the leading factor $(-1)^mq^{-\#\text{unequal}}$ survives, and it cancels the new normalization. Therefore $\psi$ and the corrections are prefix-independent, giving the actual infinity chart and the balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection; $F_A,F_0$ and the integral chart are kept separate. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 The positive-$q$ correction. Proceed down a finite dominance refinement and suppose the already constructed lower vectors $G(\mu)$ are bar-fixed. The residual in $\psi(|\lambda\rangle)-|\lambda\rangle$, after prior corrections, is $\sum_\mu r_\mu(q)G(\mu)$. Since $\psi^2=1$, each coefficient satisfies $r_\mu+\overline{r_\mu}=0$. Writing a finite antisymmetric Laurent polynomial as $r=\sum_{k>0}a_k(q^k-q^{-k})$ gives the unique $c=\sum_{k>0}a_kq^k\in q\mathbb Z[q]$ with $c-\bar c=r$. Adding $cG(\mu)$ therefore kills that residual. Induction constructs the unique bar-fixed $G(\lambda)$ with leading standard vector and remainder in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ on strictly dominated shapes. All corrections remain in the original residue multiset, so their packed abacus runners, and hence their $e$-core, are unchanged. At each degree the triangular correction matrix and its inverse are integral polynomial matrices. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F4, algebra]

3.2 The basic lower basis. On $M$ the $A$-lattice of divided node actions maps into the partition $A$-lattice because the cube matrices are Laurent-integral; its lower lattice maps into $F_0$, and the lower global basis of [F3] is bar-fixed with regular crystal residues. By the balanced-triple uniqueness of [F3] the images agree with the unique ambient $G$'s of the regular degree, so every $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ lies in $M$ and the regular family is the lower global basis of $M$; no integral splitting or saturation is assumed, and the ambient basis is not claimed component-compatible. [step 1.1, step 2.2, F3, algebra]

4.1 The false transpose symmetry. The equality $d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ fails at $e=2$ and degree $4$: the recursion gives $d_{(2,1,1),(4)}=q$ while $d_{(1,1,1,1),(3,1)}=0$, since $(2,1,1)'=(3,1)$ and $4'=(1,1,1,1)$; the source symmetry statement concerns the bar transition matrix, not the lower matrix $D$. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use $(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients need the restricted Gram inverse, which may have rational entries. [step 1.1, step 3.2, F4, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion. The explicit wedge bar is involutive, prefix-independent and integral; the global basis $G(\lambda)$ is dominance-unitriangular with $q\mathbb Z[q]$ off-diagonal coefficients and same-core support, the $A$-and $A_0$-bases and the balanced intersection are as displayed, exactly the regular family is the lower global basis of $M=V(\Lambda_0)$, and the naive transpose symmetry of $D$ is false while the correct inverse/Gram rules hold. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation
items.statement:
The assertion that the entire partition Fock module $F$ is the basic
representation, i.e. that $F=M=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle\cong
V(\Lambda_0)$ for every finite $e\ge2$, is false. For every finite $e\ge2$ the
Fock module is strictly larger than $M$: the raw basis vector $|1^e\rangle$ is
not in $M$, and its ambient lower lift $G(1^e)$ is also not in $M$. The full
field decomposition is
$F=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)}$, the $\Lambda_0$
multiplicity is $1$, and the higher constituents are nonzero; consequently the
full crystal has all partitions as vertices while its empty component is exactly
the $e$-regular partitions.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The partition Fock space with its crystal and global basis, the module $M=V(\Lambda_0)$, and the decomposition theorem.

[F1] The empty component of the full crystal is exactly the $e$-regular partitions and equals the crystal of $M$; the full crystal is a graph on all partitions; the decomposition is $F=\bigoplus_{k}V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)}$ with choice used only there ([[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F2] $M$ is the simple integrable module generated by the vacuum and receives the lower global basis of the empty component ([[prop-the-empty-partition-generates-an-integrable-highest-weight-submodule]], [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).

[F3] The top weight $\Lambda_0$ is maximal, so the top isotypic splitting of the crystal lattice gives $F_0\cap M$ with residue basis exactly the empty component; the shape $1^e$ has all parts equal and multiplicity $e$, so it is not $e$-regular ([[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]], [[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]).



## Verification

1.1 Strictness. By [F1] the full field decomposition contains the summands $V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)$ for every $k\ge0$ with multiplicity $p(k)\ge1$, and the $\Lambda_0$ summand occurs with multiplicity $p(0)=1$; since $p(k)\ge1$ for $k\ge1$ and those constituents are nonzero, $F$ is strictly larger than its $\Lambda_0$ constituent $M$. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Raw-vector exclusion. The shape $1^e$ is not $e$-regular: all its parts equal $1$ and occur $e$ times, so it lies outside the empty component by [F1]; since the residue basis of $F_0\cap M$ is exactly the empty component by [F3], every vector in $F_0\cap M$ has residue a combination of regular labels. The raw vector $|1^e\rangle$ has nonzero residue in $F_0/qF_0$ equal to the nonregular shape $1^e$, so $|1^e\rangle\notin M$; the same argument applies to $G(1^e)$, which is congruent to the same shape modulo $qF_0$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Conclusion. The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation: it has strictly more constituents than the single $V(\Lambda_0)$, and even the explicit raw and lower-lift vectors $|1^e\rangle$ and $G(1^e)$ lie outside $M$; the nonregular ambient lower vectors are not a basis of a single highest module. [step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

- The decomposition theorem used in step 1.1 is a batch-7 supplier still under
  construction at authoring time, and the Axiom of Choice is inherited through
  it; the exclusion of step 2.1 is a finite residue computation and does not
  itself use choice.

items.title: Unitriangular global basis elements at small rank
items.statement:
At $e=2$ the ambient lower basis in degrees $\le3$ is
$\varnothing\mapsto|\varnothing\rangle$, $1\mapsto|1\rangle$,
$11\mapsto|11\rangle$, $2\mapsto|2\rangle+q|11\rangle$,
$111\mapsto|111\rangle$, $3\mapsto|3\rangle+q|111\rangle$,
$21\mapsto|21\rangle$. The basic labels in these degrees are
$\varnothing,1,2,3,21$ (not $11$ or $111$). In degree $4$, rows and columns
ordered $4,31,22,211,1111$, the full lower transition matrix
$D$ (column $=G$-label, row $=$ standard shape) is

$$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0&0&0\\q&1&0&0&0\\0&q&1&0&0\\q&q^2&q&1&0\\q^2&0&0&q&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Its basic columns are $4$ and $31$. All entries lie in $\mathbb Z[q]$, the
diagonal is $1$, and off-diagonal entries lie in $q\mathbb Z[q]$, with the
proved dominance and core bounds. The apparent transpose-conjugation identity
holds accidentally for the displayed degrees $\le3$ but is **false** generally:
$d_{(211),(4)}=q$ whereas $d_{(1111),(31)}=0$. The source symmetry concerns the
bar transition matrix, not $D$. The ambient bar-fixed $G(111)$ lies outside the
basic module; no arbitrary bar-fixed combination need lie in one isotypic
summand.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The $e=2$ partition Fock space with its lower global basis, dominance order, and the node actions of the small shapes.

[F1] The lower global basis is dominance-unitriangular with $q\mathbb Z[q]$ off-diagonal coefficients, same-core support and diagonal $1$; the regular labels are the lower global basis of $M$ ([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).

[F2] Dominance is the prefix-sum order, conjugation reverses it, and the regular labels are those with part multiplicities $<2$ ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[def-regular-partition-label-convention-and-mullineux-crystal-involution]]).

[F3] The ordinary node actions on shapes of size $\le3$ are the $e=2$ table of [[ex-level-one-fock-node-actions-for-partitions-up-to-three]].

## Verification

1.1 The degrees $\le3$. Solving the triangular bar equations degree by degree with the reversal bar: in degree $2$ the only correction of $2$ is $q\,11$; in degree $3$ the partition $21$ is the only shape whose residue multiset forces no correction and $3$ receives the correction $q\,111$; the remaining shapes are bar-fixed. This gives the displayed degree-$\le3$ elements, and the basic labels are the $2$-regular ones, namely $\varnothing,1,2,3,21$, with $11$ and $111$ non-regular. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The degree-$4$ matrix. Repeating the finite bar recursion in degree $4$ gives the displayed five columns: the columns are $G(4)=|4\rangle+q|31\rangle+q|211\rangle+q^2|1111\rangle$, $G(31)=|31\rangle+q|22\rangle+q^2|211\rangle$, $G(22)=|22\rangle+q|211\rangle$, $G(211)=|211\rangle+q|1111\rangle$ and $G(1111)=|1111\rangle$, and the matrix is unitriangular with diagonal $1$; the basic columns are the regular labels $4$ and $31$. Every entry lies in $\mathbb Z[q]$ by [F1], and the dominance support is visible from the positions of the nonzero entries. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 The false transpose symmetry. Conjugation of partitions sends $211\mapsto31$ and $4\mapsto1111$, so the transpose-conjugation equality would require $d_{(211),(4)}=d_{(1111),(31)}$; but the degree-$4$ matrix gives $d_{(211),(4)}=q$ and $d_{(1111),(31)}=0$. Hence the equality fails in general; the source's symmetry statement concerns the bar transition matrix $A$, not the lower matrix $D$. [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. The displayed elements are the actual lower global basis elements in degrees $\le4$, their coefficients are integral and dominance-triangular, the basic columns are the regular labels, and the naive transpose symmetry of $D$ is refuted by the explicit pair. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
